input: Only the completed twelve-class norm-projection pilot. Do not generate new candidates or parameters.
test: For each retained coefficient-quotient basis vector, isolate each selected alpha's rational norm by stripping all prime support shared with the polynomial discriminant, coefficient denominators/contents, and the other selected norms. If the positive remainder is not a square, prove that the projected product is ramified at a good prime. This is an existential odd-valuation certificate, not a prime factorization. Certify exclusion of the whole coefficient quotient only if its dimension is at most one or all its nonzero vectors are checked; this pilot has at most one.
verification: Replay maximal-order basis combinations and norms, all finite local signatures, outside-S valuation probes, real signs, kernel dimensions and finite independence characters. Check gcd removal and nonsquareness with exact integers. Do not infer a whole-space exclusion from separately ramified basis vectors in dimension greater than one.
failure: UNKNOWN if the required nonzero quotient combinations or isolated nonsquare certificates are missing. No enlargement.
